title: glyph --ref cache: record and validate outside-root host inputs (DEC-278)
description:
Files the opum-doc ruling DEC-278 (decided 06:53Z on 2026-11-17, not escalated) on GCLI-19 item 4, the glyph --ref cache hashing arm. Filed tracker-only; NOT started. Priority is after the approved order GCLI-21, GCLI-11, GCLI-12, and the brief that starts it comes from opum-doc with a floor check. The docs scoping arm stays in place until this lands.

RULING, verbatim:
"Ruling on GCLI-19 item 4, the glyph --ref cache hashing arm: opum-doc decides B, with a bounded design.
Why B: glyph's users are agents, and they can't tell a stale warm answer from a fresh one. A cache that can disagree with a cold run after an `npm install` or a parent-tsconfig edit is a correctness defect, and documenting it doesn't help a caller who never reads the ADR. The objection to B, that the outside-root read set can't be hashed up front, falls away if the cache records that set instead of predicting it.
DESIGN (record and validate, the way build systems track dependencies):
1. On a cold build, the host wrappers in src/snapshot.ts that fall through to ts.sys (readFile, fileExists, directoryExists, for rel === null and the TypeScript library branch) record every outside-root query and its answer: a content hash for each read, and the boolean for each exists probe, NEGATIVE answers included. A newly hoisted package flips a probe from false to true, and that probe must invalidate.
2. That manifest is stored with the cache entry. computeRefKey also takes ts.version, which is cheap, and INDEX_FORMAT is bumped.
3. On a warm read, every manifest entry is re-checked before the cached index is trusted. Any mismatch, or an unreadable entry, means a cold rebuild, never a stale answer.
4. Bound: past a fixed manifest size (the writer measures a real repo and picks the cap with a reason), the run is not cached at all rather than cached unvalidated, and it says so on stderr.
5. ADR 0003 and the README then promise identity for the commit PLUS every host input the index actually read. The Consequences list keeps only what is still unhashed (indexer logic beyond INDEX_FORMAT).
6. Proof both ways, against a real repo with a hoisted dependency:
- Each of these makes the warm read rebuild: an edited parent tsconfig, an added package that a probe previously missed, a changed TypeScript version.
- With nothing changed, the warm read is served from the cache.
- Mutation control: dropping the negative-probe recording makes exactly the added-package case serve stale.
PRIORITY: after glyph-cli's approved order (GCLI-21, GCLI-11, GCLI-12), as its own task. The docs scoping arm stays in place until this lands."

Fence note (DEC-182 (1)): the design touches src/snapshot.ts, src/cache.ts and INDEX_FORMAT; a change needing a dependency, CI, pin or other fenced path class stops and reports before committing.
